103.0.0.en: Bless the Lord, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name.

103.0.1.en: 1- David calls his spirit to praise God. He encourages his soul to rise with zeal, to stand before God, to bless Him and glorify Him for His great works, even though David had passed through sufferings, but he forgets them in the flood of his joy in praising God.

103.0.2.en: 2- David affirms for the second time the praise of God, so he calls his inward parts, meaning his mind and his feelings, to glorify and bless God; that is, he praises God with his whole being, and so enjoys fellowship with Him.

103.0.3.en: 3- The meaning of this verse appears in the words of Christ when He summed up the commandments: "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart" (Mt 22:37).

103.1.0.en: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:

103.1.1.en: 1- David calls his soul to thank God for His blessings, His care and all His works with him. This confirms the importance of thanksgiving, which rejoices the heart of God.

103.1.2.en: 2- The believer in God thanks Him for His kindnesses, which are in His gifts, and also for the afflictions that come upon a person, for they are for his discipline and correction, so that they bring him near to God and pluck him out of evil; therefore he thanks God for them as well. These are the feelings of David, and of everyone who has believed and trusted in God.

103.2.0.en: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases;

103.2.1.en: 1- The first thing that deserves a person's thanks is God's forgiveness of his sins, and thereby He grants him new life. This is fulfilled in Christ the Savior in the sacrament of confession, and perhaps David saw it with the eye of prophecy.

103.2.2.en: 2- The second gift for which he thanks God is his healing from his diseases, meaning the spiritual diseases that resulted from sin, in addition to psychological and bodily diseases. For God is able to heal all diseases, and He deserves thanks and glory, for He restores a person to his first health, so that he may begin anew an active life with God.

103.3.0.en: Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies;

103.3.1.en: 1- David thanks God who rescued him from the hand of Saul and Absalom and redeemed his life, that is, saved him from death, and clothed him with a great crown by His mercy and compassion when He crowned him king over His people, and even gave him victory over his enemies. And more than this, He gave him spiritual fellowship, and he enjoyed the presence of God.

103.3.2.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about Christ the Redeemer, who by His death on the cross redeemed us from "the pit", that is, Hades and hell, into which we fall because of our sins. And He crowned us with His mercies and compassions with the crown of victory over sin and Satan. This is a pledge of the crown of eternal glory in the Kingdom.

103.3.3.en: 3- Christ redeems His children from the plots of the wicked in every generation, and keeps them in the faith, and even grants them the crowns of martyrdom, virginity, monasticism, service and the priesthood; all this by His mercies and compassions, as a free gift of love to them.

103.4.0.en: Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagle's.

103.4.1.en: 1- David also thanks God, in conclusion, for the many good things He gave him. By good things he means all material gifts, and rather the spiritual ones, so he thanks Him for keeping him, for satisfying him with material things, and for the kingdom, and he thanks Him even more for knowing Him, for choosing him in his life, and for enjoying fellowship with Him; and this is what every spiritual person ought to do.

103.4.2.en: 2- When the eagle reaches the age of thirty, its talons and its beak grow weak and the feathers of its wings stick to its body, and it is exposed to death, since it cannot seize its prey and is unable to fly. Then it must renew its strength in order to continue living, so it flies to the top of the mountain and stays there for a hundred and fifty days, that is, five months, in which it breaks its talons, once and then a second time, by striking them against the rock, and likewise its beak, and they grow again, but with strength; and it plucks out its old feathers, and others grow in their place, strong feathers not sticking to its body. It endures all these pains in order to continue its life for another thirty years, or more, for its age can reach seventy years.

103.4.3.en: 3- David wishes for his soul, when it meets spiritual coldness and weakness, that its vitality and spiritual strength be renewed through spiritual striving and suffering. Then it sets out anew in a strong life with God, as the eagle does. Then his soul is able to soar in the heaven of the virtues and to rise above earthly desires. This is what every spiritual person wishes for and strives after.

103.4.4.en: 4- Just as the eagle endures many pains to renew its youth, so the spiritual person must endure trials, and likewise the pains of spiritual striving. Also the servant endures the pains of service, so that spiritual youth may be renewed and the person may rise in his relationship with God.

103.4.5.en: 5- Thus we see that David wishes for himself, and for every one who strives spiritually, six things, which are:

103.4.6.en: a- The forgiveness of his sins.

103.4.7.en: b- The healing of his spiritual and bodily diseases.

103.4.8.en: c- Obtaining redemption from sin and eternal torment.

103.4.9.en: d- Receiving the crown of life with God and the Kingdom of Heaven.

103.4.10.en: e- Being satisfied with spiritual goods, in addition to bodily ones.

103.4.11.en: f- A continual renewal of the spiritual life.

103.4.12.en: Thanking God establishes His gifts for you, and even more and deeper blessings overflow upon you, so you live full of the grace of God, enjoying fellowship with Him, and you experience the Kingdom on earth, until you reach it in heaven.

103.5.0.en: The Lord executeth righteousness and judgment for all that are oppressed.

103.5.1.en: "Executeth": that is, carries out; its meaning is that He puts into effect righteousness and judgment and makes them prevail.

103.5.2.en: 1- God watches over all the oppressed and feels with them, and He will surely give them their right, but sometimes He postpones lifting the oppression from them, to give the oppressor an opportunity to repent, and the oppressed an opportunity to be firm in his faith and not cling to the world. But if the oppressed does not receive his right on earth, he will certainly receive it in heaven. And this is far better, that he should enjoy great delight in the Kingdom, in contrast to what awaits the oppressor, which is eternal torment.

103.5.3.en: 2- If the oppressed has lost material things, then if he takes refuge in God, He compensates him with spiritual and psychological blessings, whereas the oppressor, on the contrary, loses them.

103.5.4.en: 3- Christ our God fulfilled the divine justice on our behalf on the cross, so He removed our sins from us and gave us freedom and eternal life.

103.6.0.en: He made known his ways unto Moses, his acts unto the children of Israel.

103.6.1.en: 1- The ways of the Lord that He made known to Moses are His commandments, and His acts toward the children of Israel are His power that appeared in bringing them out of the land of Egypt by the ten plagues and in the crossing of the Red Sea.

103.6.2.en: And likewise He sustained them and kept them in the wilderness, and brought them into the land of Canaan, and they possessed it. Here His righteousness and judgment appear, and even His mercy too. For if they had endured oppression in Egypt, God rescued them from slavery, punished the oppressors, and gave them the enjoyment of His fellowship by dwelling in their midst, and even gave them the land flowing with milk and honey. And He had clearly declared to them that they should live by His ways and observe His acts when He spoke to Moses on the mountain (Ex 34:6, 7).

103.6.3.en: 2- Moses and the children of Israel knew, through His works with them, His ways, that is, His plan for salvation through His incarnation and His redemption of mankind. Just as He freed them by the ten plagues, so He endured the cross for them and redeemed them. And just as Moses and the people crossed the Red Sea, so by Baptism the believers in the New Covenant receive salvation. And likewise the rock that gives water is a type of Christ, and the victory over Amalek is a type of the victory over Satan.

103.7.0.en: 8- The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy. 9- He will not always chide: neither will he keep his anger for ever. He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities.

103.7.1.en: 1- If God is just, so that He does justice to the oppressed, then if they err, He is just also so as to repay them, but He is very long-suffering, to give them an opportunity for repentance. And He is also plenteous in mercy if they repent, so He receives them and forgives them, and even compensates them for all that they lost; as He did with Job, for after he repented of self-righteousness He compensated him with double what he had had (Job 42:10). And as He forgave Abraham for his lie and his weakness before Pharaoh, and was long-suffering toward him, and kept Sarah from the hand of Pharaoh (Gen 20:3-7). And as He was long-suffering toward His people in the age of the Judges, and when the enemies humbled them He sent them judges, such as Gideon and Samson, and saved them from slavery.

103.7.2.en: 2- God does not continue His punishment of those who err, so that He would appear to be holding a grudge against them; the meaning of "keep his anger" is His anger against them. But He disciplines His children so that they may repent, and then He has mercy on them and forgives them.

103.8.0.en: 11- For as the heaven is high above the earth, so great is his mercy toward them that fear him.

103.8.1.en: 12- As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us. 13- Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.

103.8.2.en: 1- The children of God are those who fear Him, so they keep away from sin, and if they sin they hasten to repentance.

103.8.3.en: And those who always strive toward Him to live by His commandments and adorn themselves with the virtues, God singles out and gives them great mercy, very strong, and even beyond comprehension in its size, for it is unlimited. So he likens it to its height being like the height of heaven above the earth, and also like the distance of the east from the west.

103.8.4.en: He removes our sins from us, and for this reason we renounce Satan and his sins in Baptism facing the west, while the confession of Christ is made facing the east, that we may live for Him.

103.8.5.en: 2- God's mercy appears in the heavens, for they cover the earth on every side, and His mercies overflow in them; that is, the light from the sun, the moon and the stars, the air we breathe, and the rains that water us and water the crops.

103.8.6.en: 3- The writer of the Psalm explains God's great mercy by saying that it comes upon us from God because He is our Father, so He has compassion on us, and even if we sin He is long-suffering so that we may repent. And we cannot understand the wisdom of our loving, compassionate Father, who seems harsh in His discipline, although He is merciful and wants to remove our sins from us and bring us back to Him. And sometimes He delays His blessings, and then pours out mercies that surpass our understanding. His wisdom is far higher than we are, like the heaven, of which we can understand only a little, and about the movement of the planets and the stars in it, the winds and the mist; these are very difficult for our understanding, so truly "how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!" (Rom 11:33).

103.8.7.en: 4- The son who loves and fears his father trusts in his fatherhood, so he surrenders himself into his hands, submitting to his will because of his faith that his father arranges good for him; even if he does not understand the things that pass through his life, or the afflictions that come upon him, yet he is at all times at rest in his father's arms.

103.9.0.en: 14- For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust.

103.9.1.en: As a flower of the field, so he flourisheth. 16- For the wind passeth over it, and it is gone; and the place thereof shall know it no more.

103.9.2.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm appeals for God's mercies, so he declares to Him that man is weak, indeed nothing before the greatness of God, and very liable to error, and he likens him to dust, and likewise to the grass that grows and flowers, then the strong wind comes upon it, uproots it and scatters it everywhere. By the wind he means trials and death. And since man is weak to this degree, he needs the great mercy of God to support him, forgive him and receive him.

103.9.3.en: 2- If man is weak to this degree, he ought to humble himself before God and trust in Him, and even hold fast to Him by faith in all his steps, for he always needs God's support. And on the other hand, he should have compassion on the people around him when they err, and not judge them, so that he deserves God's mercies.

103.10.0.en: 17- But the mercy of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear him, and his righteousness unto children's children;

103.10.1.en: 18- To such as keep his covenant, and to those that remember his commandments to do them.

103.10.2.en: 1- God's mercy is constant throughout life, and for ever, and generous and strong, but it is given only to those who have the following:

103.10.3.en: a- The fear of God, which keeps them from evil.

103.10.4.en: b- Those who hold fast to God's covenant, that they may live for Him.

103.10.5.en: c- Those who always remember God's commandments in order to put them into practice in their lives.

103.10.6.en: 2- Likewise God's righteousness does justice to His oppressed children and rewards them for all their toil with peace and inner joy, and many blessings in life, then the glories of eternity. All this is given not only to the children but also to their children who live as they do as children of God. Likewise "children's children" means the works of the person and his spiritual striving, and for the sake of these works God blesses the children and keeps them by His righteousness, and God's righteousness is completed in the happiness that He gives His children in eternity as a reward to them for their good works.

103.10.7.en: If God's mercy and long-suffering, my brother, are great to this degree, this urges you to repentance and to strive toward every good work. And do not be troubled by the warfare of the demons and the fluctuations of the world and its fears, for God's mercy and righteousness support you, so you walk with firm steps toward the Kingdom, enjoying the care of your tender Father.

103.11.0.en: 19- The Lord hath prepared his throne in the heavens; and his kingdom ruleth over all.

103.11.1.en: 1- The throne of God and His place in heaven are firm for the following reasons:

103.11.2.en: a- Heaven rises above the earth with all its desires and material things, for it is a symbol of spirituality.

103.11.3.en: b- Heaven is firm, not like the changeable earth, for human beings are changeable in their characters and their behavior.

103.11.4.en: c- Heaven is mysterious, a symbol of the existence of God; for He is unlimited, and the mind cannot grasp all that is in Him.

103.11.5.en: 2- God is the King of kings, and His kingdom rules over all people, for He is the Upholder of all, the Creator of all creatures and their Ruler. Therefore, of course, people ought to submit to Him and obey His commandments.

103.12.0.en: 20- Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word. 21- Bless ye the Lord, all ye his hosts; ye ministers of his, that do his pleasure.

103.12.1.en: 1- The great God who dwells in the heavens is glorified by the angels, and these are distinguished by the following:

103.12.2.en: a- They belong to God and are set apart for Him ("his angels").

103.12.3.en: b- They have great strength that gives them the ability to do many services for God, far above the strength of human beings.

103.12.4.en: c- They are obedient to God's commands and submissive to Him.

103.12.5.en: 2- God also blesses His hosts, and they are the believers in God on earth, who share with the angels in praising God and serving Him, and strive to please Him by keeping His commandments and keeping away from all evil.

103.13.0.en: 22- Bless the Lord, all his works in all places of his dominion: bless the Lord, O my soul.

103.13.1.en: 1- In conclusion he calls on all the works of the Lord to bless Him and praise Him because of His greatness. And God's works include not only the angels and human beings, but also all creatures, living and inanimate. For all of them praise Him by following the order that God created for them. And the leader of creation, who is man, leads it in praise by his obedience to God and his prayers.

103.13.2.en: 2- He ends the Psalm by calling his soul to bless God and praise Him, as he began the Psalm; that is, the life of man from its beginning to its end ought to be filled with praise and thanksgiving to God, just as all eternity is praise.

103.13.3.en: The most important of your works on earth is prayer and the praise of God; when you become skilled in it, you deserve to join the heavenly worshippers and to enjoy the vision of God.

103.13.4.en: God the glorified Creator: "Bless the Lord, O my soul. O Lord my God, thou art very great" (v. 1). Introduction:

103.13.5.en: 1- Its writer: This Psalm has no title, that is, it is one of the "orphan" Psalms, but the Septuagint attributes it to David.

103.13.6.en: 2- There is a similarity between this Psalm and the one before it, for both praise God, but the preceding Psalm praises Him for His mercy with His people, whereas this Psalm shows God's care for the whole of nature.

103.13.7.en: 3- This Psalm is also similar to the first and second chapters of the Book of Genesis, but it is to be noted that the Book of Genesis concentrates on the creation that God created, whereas this Psalm concentrates on the greatness of the Creator who cares for all creation.

103.13.8.en: 4- This Psalm is liturgical; the Jews used to chant it on the morning of the great Day of Atonement, when God permits the high priest to enter the Holy of Holies, because this day is a symbol of the renewal of creation, as the Psalm mentions (v. 30), and it is a symbol of the great Friday on which our High Priest, Christ our God, offered Himself and redeemed us on the cross; therefore we declare that He is the Creator and Shepherd of all creation, and we glorify Him.

103.13.9.en: 5- There is a similarity between this Psalm and Psalm 19 (Ps 19), because both show God the great Creator who cares for His creation and is glorified in it.

103.13.10.en: 6- This Psalm does not occur in the prayers of the Agpeya.
